name: Bajaj Finserv Ltd
title: Bajaj Finserv Ltd - 532978 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Diversified financial holding with insurance-led earnings; GI combined ratio 104.7% and PAT down to INR 478 crore on lower realised gains, while Life VNB rose 87% to INR 271 crore with NBM 15.9%.

summary.headline: Bajaj Finserv Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 18% to INR 6,297 crore on total income up 19% to INR 42,037 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income grew 19% to INR 42,037 crore and PAT grew 18% to INR 6,297 crore, per management. Lending subsidiaries (Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Housing) posted strong growth, with Bajaj Finance PAT up about 27.6%. Insurance profits fell sharply as lower realised capital gains and the GST impact on Life acquisition costs hit reported earnings, while Bajaj General's combined ratio rose to about 104.7% on Ind AS-basis reporting. Management also announced approval to set up a reinsurance company.

segments.name: Bajaj General Insurance
segments.commentary: GWP up 11.3% to INR 5,789 crore, in line with industry GDPI of 11.1%; ex-crop and government health, GWP grew about 10% vs industry about 12%, with motor tactically reduced. Underwriting loss about INR 130 crore vs INR 116 crore; annualised ROE 17.3% ex-surplus capital at 200% solvency.

segments.name: Bajaj Life Insurance
segments.commentary: Retail protection 12% of retail business, growing 60% YoY; group protection up 95%. GWP up 35% on renewal premium growth of about 18%; persistency dipped in certain cohorts. Solvency 285%. AUM INR 1,43,744 crore, up almost 10%.

segments.name: Bajaj Finance and Bajaj Housing Finance
segments.commentary: Bajaj Finance new loans up 20% to 1.61 crore; GNPA 0.96%, NNPA 0.39%, CRAR 20.9%, opex to NTI 33.4%. Bajaj Housing AUM up 24%, GNPA 0.29%, NNPA 0.12%, CRAR 21.59%, PAT up 23% to INR 715 crore.

segments.name: Bajaj Finserv Direct (Bajaj Markets)
segments.commentary: Bajaj Markets disbursement about INR 2,269 crore (vs INR 1,209 crore last year); operating revenue INR 107 crore, up 32%, including about INR 15 crore trail revenue; 103 unique partners. Management targets breakeven in Q3 or Q4 FY27 on a quarterly basis.

segments.name: Bajaj Finserv Health
segments.commentary: About 6 million healthcare transactions vs 5.6 million last year, but revenue declined slightly due to partnership restructuring under RBI NBFC business-conduct rules. Provider network of about 1.3 lakh doctors, 15,000+ hospitals, about 7,000 lab touch points. Breakeven targeted for Q3 or Q4 FY28.

segments.name: Bajaj Asset Management
segments.commentary: AUM INR 31,444 crore, up 26%, 26th-ranked MF company; equity mix 63%; SIP book up 66% and SIP folios up 69%. Management targets INR 1 lakh crore AUM in about three years as path to profitability.

guidance_outlook: Bajaj Finserv Direct expected to break even on a quarterly basis in Q3 or Q4 FY27 and on a full-year basis in FY28.
Bajaj Finserv Health expected to break even in Q3 or Q4 FY28, full-year breakeven the year after.
Bajaj Finance expects opex to NTI to improve by about 25 to 40 bps in FY27.
Bajaj General expects reported combined ratio to remain best in industry despite pricing pressure; Ind AS transition from 1 April 2027 expected to release large discounting benefit on TP liabilities.
Capital needs: Health about INR 200-300 crore over next 6 quarters; AMC modest; largest chunk to ALTs and reinsurance company (phase 1 domestic, phase 2 international after 3-year rating process).
capex_capacity: Board approved setting up a reinsurance company; regulatory approvals to be sought, capital not yet quantified.
Alternate investments business commenced with PMS launch; real estate and AI AIF launches expected in the coming quarter.
Insurance companies move to Ind AS from 1 April 2027 after IRDAI forbearance; acquisition costs to be amortised rather than upfronted.
Bajaj General paid high dividend and bought back shares in prior quarter, reducing capital by about INR 3,515 crore.
demand_pricing: Industry general insurance soft pricing; management says Bajaj General combined ratio deterioration is about 1 pp vs 5% or more at peers, and it outperforms market by 16-18%.
Bajaj General reduced motor exposure tactically due to elevated pricing pressure; motor own damage loss ratios rising industry-wide.
Crop business tenders expected to be higher than last year; government health contract 2+1 with lives covered likely lower than last year's base.
Life product mix: ULIP about 45%, par 22-25%, non-par plus annuity 22-25%, retail protection 12%; 34% of customers onboarded with term plans and 22% of NOPs with riders.
Bajaj Markets: 50-plus lenders on platform; 35 products; personal loans lead, gold and home loans growing fast.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Supreme Court ruling on motor third-party compensation for homemakers and reserving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 30,000 figure may not apply; TP ultimate loss ratios assumed are conservative and build in buffer, and homemaker cases are very few. Industry is seeking a TP price hike. GIC has filed a review petition.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of monsoon and natural catastrophes on motor, commercial and crop; road to profitability for subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said soft market means pricing below average, but Bajaj General's CR deterioration is only about 1 pp. Treaties are robust and NATCAT reserves are maintained. Breakeven timelines: Finserv Direct Q3/Q4 FY27, Health Q3/Q4 FY28, AMC targeting INR 1 lakh crore AUM in 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did group protection grow nearly 100%, and how do annuity and non-par relate; how is GST impact absorbed?
qa_highlights.answer: Tarun Chugh said MFI revival and 20+ new partners added in 15 months drove growth; annuity and non-par share a chassis, non-par was reconfigured after persistency hit. Margin expansion came from riders at same commission, product mix and cost savings under Bajaj Life 2.0.

qa_highlights.question: Trajectory of crop and government health tender businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Tapan Singhel said crop tenders this year would exceed last year; government health is a 2+1 contract so renewal is automatic, though base may be somewhat lower than last year.

qa_highlights.question: Reinsurance capital requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramandeep Sahni said the project is at drawing-board stage; phase 1 domestic needs limited capital, phase 2 international after about 3-year ratings process needs more; not yet quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Ind AS transition impact and rider attachment?
qa_highlights.answer: Effective date 1 April 2027 after one-year forbearance. Key impacts: acquisition cost amortisation for both insurers; GI TP liabilities discounting could release large amount; onerous contract recognition could benefit GI. Riders attached to 22% of NOPs.

qa_highlights.question: Motor own damage loss ratio drivers and FY27 strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Avais Karmali said the rise is industry-wide and management is slowing motor on risk selection; no segment-level breakdown given, as pricing is micro-segmented geography-wise.

risks_watch: Soft general insurance pricing and monsoon/NATCAT losses could raise industry loss ratios and pressure Bajaj General margins.
Ind AS transition from 1 April 2027 and regulatory clarifications on onerous contracts and discounting remain open; quantification pending.
Supreme Court motor TP homemaker ruling; GIC review petition pending; TP price hike still awaited.
Life persistency dips in certain cohorts; GST impact on margins; lower realised capital gains depressed profit.
Bajaj Finserv Direct and Health breakeven timelines depend on partner restructuring under RBI digital lending and NBFC rules.
summary.management_tone: Confident on lending and Bajaj Life growth and on relative underwriting outperformance, but cautious on the soft general insurance market and the cycle. Evasive on segment-level motor own damage loss drivers and on specific Ind AS impact quantification, deferring to future clarity.
key_quotes: Despite that, we believe that the reported COR would be the best in the industry despite the stress in the market in terms of pricing.
So, I don't think that we should get too nervous about the Supreme Court ruling.
Bajaj General, even in soft markets has consistently outperformed the market.
And now 34% of our customers last quarter were only onboarded with term plans.

growth.why: Consolidated total income +19% and PAT +18% YoY, with Bajaj Finance AUM +24% and new loans +20%; guidance includes Bajaj Finance opex-to-NTI improving 25-40 bps in FY27, Bajaj Markets quarterly breakeven in Q3/Q4 FY27, and an AMC target of INR 1 lakh crore AUM in three years, backed mainly by existing franchise momentum and product launches rather than quantified capacity.
